name: Question 10
problem: Find a vector equation of the line that passes through the points $C(-1,0,4)$ and $D(-7,2,11).$
worked_solution:
The vector equation of the straight line passing through $C$ and parallel to $v$ is given by

$$
r=c+tv,
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty )$ and $c$ is the position vector of $C.$ 

We can find a direction vector by computing the displacement vector between the given points $C(-1,0,4)$ and $D(-7,2,11)$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\overset{\to }{CD} \\  & =⟨-7,2,11⟩-⟨-1,0,4⟩ \\  & =⟨-6,2,7⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the vector equation of the line is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ 4\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ 2 \\ 7\end{aligned}],\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

Question 10

Find a vector equation of the line that passes through the points C(−1,0,4) and D(−7,2,11).

a
 r=[−104]+t[62−7],t∈(−∞,∞)
b
 r=[40−1]+t[−627],t∈(−∞,∞)
c
r=[−104]+t[−627],t∈(−∞,∞)
d
 r=[−104]+t[2−67],t∈(−∞,∞)
e
 r=[10−4]+t[−627],t∈(−∞,∞)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The vector equation of the straight line passing through C and parallel to v is given by r=c+tv, where t∈(−∞,∞) and c is the position vector of C.

We can find a direction vector by computing the displacement vector between the given points C(−1,0,4) and D(−7,2,11), as follows:

v=CD→=⟨−7,2,11⟩−⟨−1,0,4⟩=⟨−6,2,7⟩

Therefore, the vector equation of the line is given by

r=[−104]+t[−627],t∈(−∞,∞).
